## Overview

FHIR R4 is the dominant standard for healthcare data exchange.
`live_fhir()`:

- pushes `==`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `%in%` and `grepl()` filters to the FHIR
  search API;
- follows FHIR Bundle pagination (`Bundle.link[relation=next]`);
- evaluates FHIRPath expressions in the schema map to flatten nested fields.

## Creating a FHIR connection

```{r connection}
library(ontologyConnectR)
library(dplyr)

patient_con <- live_fhir(
  schema_map = list(
    Patient = list(
      resource = "Patient",
      pk       = "patient_id",
      columns  = list(
        patient_id  = "id",
        family_name = "name.where(use='official').family",
        given_name  = "name.where(use='official').given.first()",
        birth_date  = "birthDate",
        gender      = "gender"
      )
    )
  ),
  base_url = "https://hapi.fhir.org/baseR4"
)
```

## Building the context

```{r context}
library(ontologySpecR)

patient <- object_type(
  "Patient",
  properties = list(
    property_def("patient_id", "string"),
    property_def("family_name", "string"),
    property_def("given_name", "string"),
    property_def("birth_date", "date"),
    property_def("gender", "string")
  ),
  primary_key = "patient_id"
)

ctx <- connect_context(
  bundle("clinical", "1.0.0", objects = list(patient)),
  live_connections = list(Patient = patient_con)
)
```

## Querying with filter push-down

```{r query}
# Both filters go to the server: ?birthdate=gt1990-01-01&gender=female
result <- connect_object_set(ctx, "Patient") |>
  filter(birth_date > "1990-01-01", gender == "female") |>
  head(20) |>
  collect()
```

| dplyr filter | FHIR search modifier | Example URL parameter     |
|--------------|----------------------|---------------------------|
| `==`         | exact match          | `?family=Smith`           |
| `grepl()`    | `:contains`          | `?family:contains=smi`    |
| `>`          | `gt` prefix          | `?birthdate=gt1990-01-01` |
| `>=`         | `ge` prefix          | `?birthdate=ge1990-01-01` |
| `<`          | `lt` prefix          | `?birthdate=lt2000-01-01` |
| `<=`         | `le` prefix          | `?birthdate=le2000-01-01` |
| `%in%`       | comma-separated      | `?status=active,inactive` |

## Using objectSetsR instead

The connection is a DBI connection, so it also works with objectSetsR,
called fully qualified:

```{r objectsetsr}
os_ctx <- objectSetsR::ontology_context(
  bundle("clinical", "1.0.0", objects = list(patient)),
  patient_con
)
objectSetsR::object_set(os_ctx, "Patient")
```

## Authentication and caching

```{r auth}
secured_con <- live_fhir(
  schema_map = list(Patient = list(resource = "Patient", pk = "patient_id",
                                   columns = list(patient_id = "id"))),
  base_url  = "https://fhir.example.org/R4",
  auth      = conn_auth_bearer(env_var = "FHIR_TOKEN"),
  cache_ttl = 3600L   # cache for 1 hour
)
```
